summary: Round 10. R9-1 is fixed the right way: scripts/check-io-seam.sh's header now carries no package count and no enumeration. R9-3's narrowed sentence is TRUE -- I re-measured the anchoring in both directions. M0.112's four claims are all TRUE -- I re-measured every one. Nothing round 9 verified was broken: the three backlog rows are four-cell and well-formed, the eleven-vs-two implements measurement still holds, ALLOWED and PACKAGES are unchanged. But the sentence that replaced the stale count asserts something the same commit contradicts three times: it calls io_seam_scan.py's PACKAGES 'the only copy of it' while AGENTS.md:153-156, code-structure.md:20-23 and the M0.107 backlog cell each hold a full twelve-name enumeration WITH the count, two of them added by this commit. That is false at these bytes and it is the same defect class, relocated: it tells the next maintainer there is one place to edit, and M0.112 -- also in this commit -- schedules the PACKAGES growth that makes the other three stale. The remedy is deleting five words, NOT rewriting the header; every previous round's rewrite produced the next round's finding. No object-store request is added or changed: the gate is a static text scan at the pre-commit stage, so its cost scales with source files at commit time and with nothing at runtime.

findings.title: check-io-seam.sh calls PACKAGES 'the only copy of it'; the same commit adds two more full copies and a third already exists
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a throwaway worktree at the staged bytes. scripts/check-io-seam.sh line 7 reads "`io_seam_scan.py`'s `PACKAGES` is the list and the only copy of it -- NO COUNT AND NO ENUMERATION APPEARS HERE, because this header carried both and went stale the round after the list grew, for the ninth recurrence of one defect class on this task." The removal of the count and the enumeration from this header is correct and answers R9-1 exactly as it should have been answered. The sole-copy claim is false. `grep -n 'twelve' AGENTS.md docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md docs/internal/product/backlog.md` finds three more copies, each with the count AND all twelve names: AGENTS.md:153-156 ('It bans twelve I/O PACKAGES outright -- `java.nio.file`, ... `javax.net`'), docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md:20-23 ('The gate bans twelve I/O PACKAGES outright -- ...'), and the M0.107 backlog cell:45 ('TWELVE I/O PACKAGES ARE BANNED OUTRIGHT ... are forbidden as PACKAGES'). All three are ACCURATE today -- I confirmed each enumerates the same twelve that `python3 -c 'import io_seam_scan; print(io_seam_scan.PACKAGES)'` prints -- and the AGENTS.md and code-structure.md copies are ADDED BY THIS DIFF. Consequence a reader suffers, and it is scheduled rather than hypothetical: the header's own next paragraph says 'Each PACKAGE a reach can live in must be named, and the list grows when a reader finds one', and M0.112 -- added by this same commit -- names the two packages that will grow it (`javax.xml.parsers`, `java.rmi`), which I re-measured as still passing. A maintainer who lands M0.112 reads 'the only copy of it', edits PACKAGES alone, and leaves AGENTS.md -- the document loaded into EVERY session -- saying 'twelve' and listing twelve of fourteen. No gate catches that; `check-io-seam.sh` derives its printed constant from `len(io_seam_scan.BAN_ENTRIES)` and `IoSeamGateTest` checks its sample table against `ALL_ENTRIES`, but nothing checks any prose enumeration against `PACKAGES`. This is round 9's finding one hop removed: a claim about the list that the tree beside it falsifies, written by the round whose subject was that claim. FIX, AND IT MUST BE A DELETION: strike 'and the only copy of it' from line 7, leaving '`io_seam_scan.py`'s `PACKAGES` is the list -- NO COUNT AND NO ENUMERATION APPEARS HERE, because ...'. Do NOT rewrite the header or restate the relationship between the four documents; adding prose about prose is what carried this task from round 3 to round 10. If the three copies are to be recorded as work, one clause appended to the existing M0.112 row ('and the twelve-name enumerations in AGENTS.md, code-structure.md and this cell go stale when PACKAGES grows') is the whole of it -- the better fix, cutting those enumerations down to a pointer, is a docs change that is not this task's.

findings.title: R9-5's wrong denominator survives and is not among the four minors M0.112 records
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED at the staged bytes: the M0.107 cell still reads 'a one-off test here would cover one class of forty and make the absence look closed', while `git ls-files -- '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java' | grep -vc '^binstore-backends/'` prints 101 and IoSeamGateTest's class javadoc makes the same argument as 'one class of a hundred'. I raised this as R9-5, judged it minor and wrote that it was 'not worth a round of its own'; that judgement stands and I am not reversing it. Recording it only because M0.112 captures four of round 9's five minors and this is the one it drops, so it is now in no row and in no fix -- which is how a known-wrong number becomes a number nobody remembers questioning. NOT BLOCKING: the argument the denominator supports (a per-class test covers a vanishing fraction) holds at 40, 101 or 1000, the number is not marked MEASURED, and the cell is prose about why the task carries an M0 number rather than a claim about what the gate does. Either change 'forty' to 'a hundred' if the cell is being edited for R10-1 anyway, or add the word to M0.112's list. Do not open a round for it.

verified_from_previous_round: R9-1 FIXED, and by deletion rather than by a new number: scripts/check-io-seam.sh:6-12 now names no count and enumerates no package, and points at io_seam_scan.py's PACKAGES. The one thing wrong with the replacement sentence is R10-1.

R9-3 FIXED and the narrowed sentence is TRUE. Verified against _shape and EXPLICIT at the staged bytes: '.now()' takes the endswith('()') arm with an empty owner, giving head = r'\b[A-Z][\w$]*'; '.now(...)' is not built by _shape at all but by EXPLICIT, r'\b[A-Z][\w$]*\s*\.\s*now\s*\(...'. Both anchor a capitalised receiver, so the cell's claim about those two entries specifically is correct. MEASURED: 'class Uses2 { Object go(Window w) { return w.now(); } }' scans clean. MEASURED the paired claim: 'class Uses { long go(Tick t) { return t.nanoTime(); } }' is refused, 'nanoTime( reaches the real clock directly', in a file touching no clock. One nuance the cell overstates without being false -- the record COMPONENT DECLARATION alone is not refused ('record Tick(long nanoTime, long seq) { }' scans clean, because there is no '(' after the name); what is refused is every call of the generated accessor, so the component is unusable in business logic and the stated consequence holds. Not worth a word.

M0.112(a) TRUE, MEASURED: one file importing java.io.BufferedInputStream and java.io.EOFException and using both is refused twice, 'java.io reaches the filesystem directly' at each import line. Neither type is in ALLOWED.

M0.112(b) TRUE, MEASURED: one file calling javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().newDocumentBuilder().parse(s) and java.rmi.Naming.lookup(s) scans clean -- 0 violations. Neither package is in PACKAGES and neither call shape is in BANNED.

M0.112(c) TRUE: 'currentTimeMillis(' and 'nanoTime(' contain no '.', so _shape takes the bare-call arm and builds an unanchored r'(?:\bnanoTime\s*\(|::\s*nanoTime\b)'. The row's statement that anchoring them would reopen the static-import escape is correct -- there is no receiver in 'import static java.lang.System.*; ... nanoTime()' to anchor to.

M0.112's framing TRUE: each addition to ALLOWED or PACKAGES does need a sample, because everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED asserts containsExactlyInAnyOrder against io_seam_scan.ALL_ENTRIES, which is BAN_ENTRIES plus 'allow:'-prefixed ALLOWED.

NOTHING BROKEN that round 9 had verified. The three backlog rows touched (M0.107, M0.109, M0.112) each hold exactly 4 unescaped-pipe cells against the 4-column header and end with a pipe; no orphan non-pipe line sits inside any table, so the M0.109 defect shapes are absent. The header's 'ELEVEN src/main files match implements .*(BinStore|Sequencer|SubscriptionTransport|Membership|Clock) against this module's TWO' re-measured as exactly 11 and 2. PACKAGES is 12, BAN_ENTRIES 28, ALL_ENTRIES 48; AGENTS.md, code-structure.md and the backlog cell all enumerate the same twelve, so no count in the tree is wrong TODAY.
